revision: r2 (2026-11-10): the r1 critic's must-fixes applied (reviews/r1-critic.md), plus the cold-read fixes + the r1 continuity must-fixes (reviews/r1-continuity.md) + r2 critic leftovers (reviews/r2-critic.md)
caption: grandpa broke the same lectern 3,000 times 📚
logline: A grandpa has broken the same librarian's lectern three thousand times; his grandkid knows Grandma lives on the island across the bay and told him to walk there or not come at all.
question: why tf has grandpa broken the same lectern 3,000 times?
premise: Grandpa has broken the same lectern three thousand times: the librarian holds up a book, he reads it, 'Not THAT one', and breaks the lectern again. Grandma lives on the island across the bay; her window is lit every night. He won't take a boat or build a bridge, ten years. When she left, she told him: walk the water to me, or don't come.
twist: He's been re-rolling the librarian for one book, Frost Walker (vanilla: breaking a librarian's lectern before you trade changes the book she offers; Frost Walker freezes water under your feet). She meant 'never'; he took it literally. This morning the librarian holds up a new book, the trade screen reads Frost Walker II, and Grandpa says nothing: he walks off the end of the dock and the sea freezes under every step, a white path toward the lit window. Cut.
